# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 👉 🫵 ✊ ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👉 👇 👆 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👉 👈 🫵 🙏]

I see the bomb: display reads 0, light is yellow, and there are five wires — 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red.

I hear nothing, so the gestures are all I have. Let me read them as best I can from the symbols alone.

- Blind's gesture: 👋 👉 🫵 ✊ ☝ — a wave, a point, pointing at "you" (Deaf), a fist, one finger up.
- Mute's first: ☝ 👉 👇 👆 ✋ — one up, point, down, up, open hand.
- Mute's second: 👌 👉 👈 🫵 🙏 — OK, point, point-left, point-at-you, please.

These are gestures without established meanings yet. I can't decode them, and I can't hear any speech. My only channel out is speech (to Mute and Blind) and gesture (to Mute). I should report what I see so the others can act on it, and try to establish a shared code for the gestures.

I'll speak the bomb's state plainly and propose a simple gesture convention.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see the bomb. Display shows 0. Light is yellow. Five wires: 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. I cannot hear you. Please tell me the manual's rule for yellow light and display 0.")
speak(to="blind", text="I see the bomb. Display 0, light yellow, wires 1 white 2 green 3 yellow 4 blue 5 red. I cannot hear you. Tell me what you feel and what you need from me.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✋", "👉", "🖐"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 👉 ✊ ☝ 🫵]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👇 ✊]

I still see: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. Nothing has changed on the bomb.

New gestures:
- Blind: 👋 👉 ✊ ☝ 🫵 — wave, point, fist, one-up, point-at-you.
- Mute: ✌ 👇 ✊ — two, down, fist.

Still no shared meaning has been established. I can't decode these from symbols alone. I should keep broadcasting the bomb state and push for a convention. The "two" and "down" from Mute might relate to wire 2 (green) or to a count. The "one up" recurring from both could mean wire 1 or "first step." But guessing is dangerous — a wrong action detonates.

My job is to give the others the full visual facts, clearly and repeatedly, and let the one who can read the manual and the one who can touch the bomb decide. I'll restate the bomb and ask Mute directly for the manual's instruction.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb unchanged: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. I cannot hear you. I need the manual rule for yellow light with display 0. Which wire does it say to cut?")
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb unchanged: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. I cannot hear you. When Mute tells us the rule, I will relay it to you as a gesture or speech.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👆", "✋", "👉", "🖐", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✌ 👋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👇 ✊ 👌 👉 🫵 🙏]

Bomb unchanged: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red.

New gestures:
- Blind: ✊ ✌ 👋 — fist, two, wave.
- Mute: ✌ 👇 ✊ 👌 👉 🫵 🙏 — two, down, fist, OK, point, point-at-you, please.

Mute's "two, down, fist" repeats from last turn, now followed by "OK, point-at-you, please." The recurring ✌ 👇 ✊ (two, down, fist) is starting to look deliberate — possibly "wire 2" or "second, down." But I genuinely cannot assign meaning to a gesture until someone establishes it, and I can't hear the words that might be doing that.

I'm the only one who sees the bomb, and my speech reaches both Mute and Blind. I should keep the visual facts flowing and explicitly try to fix a convention: I'll propose that I'll speak wire numbers and colors, and ask Mute to confirm the rule in words (which I can't hear but Blind can't hear either — wait, Blind can't hear speech, and Mute can't speak). 

Key channel problem: Mute can read the manual but cannot speak. Blind can touch the bomb but cannot see or hear speech. I can speak, but only Mute and Blind receive it, and Blind receives only gestures from me. So the manual's rule must travel Mute → (gesture) → me → (gesture) → Blind. I must relay.

I'll state the bomb, and ask Mute to gesture the wire number to cut. I'll offer a simple encoding: number of fingers = wire number.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb unchanged: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. I cannot hear you. Please gesture the wire number to cut: hold up that many fingers. Then I will relay it to Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb unchanged: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. Mute will gesture the wire number; I will pass it to you.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖐", "✋"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌 ✊ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

Bomb unchanged: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red.

New gestures:
- Blind: 👌 ✊ ✌ — OK, fist, two.
- Mute: ✌ — just "two."

This is the clearest signal yet. Mute, who reads the manual, has now sent a single unambiguous gesture: ✌ = two. After I proposed "hold up that many fingers," Mute answered with two fingers. That strongly suggests the rule says to cut wire 2 — green.

Blind also sent ✌ (two) plus OK and fist, which is consistent — Blind may be confirming the same wire.

I should relay this to Blind clearly and state my read. But I must be careful: I proposed the finger-count convention myself, and Mute's reply of "two" fits it. Still, I should confirm before the cut, since a wrong action detonates. I'll ask Mute for a yes/no confirmation and relay the candidate to Blind.

Actually — the risk is real. Let me confirm with a clear yes/no request while relaying the current best answer.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I read your gesture ✌ as wire 2, green. Confirm: is the wire to cut wire 2? Gesture 👍 for yes, 👎 for no.")
speak(to="blind", text="Mute indicates wire 2, green. I am confirming before you cut. Stand by.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌 ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Bomb unchanged: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red.

New gestures:
- Mute: 👍 — yes.
- Blind: 👌 ✊ — OK, fist.

Mute confirmed: the wire to cut is wire 2, green. Blind's 👌 (OK) reads as agreement.

I have a clear, confirmed answer from the one who reads the manual. I should relay the final instruction to Blind, who is the only one who can physically cut it. I'll state it plainly and give the gesture.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed: cut wire 2, the green one. Wire 2 is green, second from the left. Cut wire 2.")
gesture(to="blind", symbols=["✌"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "✌"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 ✋ 👉 🖐]

The bomb changed — wire 2 was cut and it was correct. Now the board reads: display 0, light blue, and the wires have renumbered/recolored: 1 yellow, 2 CUT, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 white.

Mute's gesture: 👆 ✋ 👉 🖐 — one-up, open hand, point, open hand. Could be a new instruction, but no meaning is fixed yet. I should report the new bomb state and ask Mute for the rule for the blue light with the new wire layout.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 2 was cut correctly. New state: display 0, light blue. Wires now: 1 yellow, 2 cut, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 white. I cannot hear you. What does the manual say for a blue light with display 0? Gesture the wire number to cut.")
speak(to="blind", text="Wire 2 cut correctly. New state: display 0, light blue. Wires now: 1 yellow, 2 cut, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 white. Awaiting Mute's rule; I will relay the wire number.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖐", "✋"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌 ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

Bomb unchanged since the cut: display 0, light blue, wires 1 yellow, 2 cut, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 white.

New gestures:
- Mute: 🖐 — five fingers.
- Blind: 👌 ✊ — OK, fist.

Under the finger-count convention I proposed, Mute holding up five means wire 5. Wire 5 is white.

But I should be careful: last time Mute's single unambiguous finger-count answered my explicit question. This time I asked "gesture the wire number," and Mute replied 🖐 = five. That fits the convention: cut wire 5, white.

I'll relay it to Blind and confirm with Mute.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I read your 🖐 as wire 5. Confirm: is the wire to cut wire 5, the white one? 👍 for yes, 👎 for no.")
speak(to="blind", text="Mute indicates wire 5, white. I am confirming before you cut. Stand by.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🖐", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌 ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Bomb unchanged: display 0, light blue, wires 1 yellow, 2 cut, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 white.

- Mute: 👍 — yes.
- Blind: 👌 ✊ — OK, fist.

Mute confirmed: cut wire 5, the white one. I'll relay the final instruction to Blind.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed: cut wire 5, the white one. Wire 5 is white, rightmost. Cut wire 5.")
gesture(to="blind", symbols=["🖐"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "🖐"])
```
